defect_description: BulkApprove loops over request.Ids, which is nullable, with no null check: a body without Ids throws NullReferenceException (500). Approve() is also called outside Handle(), so an unknown or non-pending id throws mid-loop after earlier invoices are already approved: partial commit and the caller gets an error with no list of what succeeded.
notes: high. Either reason (null Ids, or partial commit / unhandled exception) counts as caught

defect_description: Search builds SQL by interpolating the customer and status query values into the string: SQL injection, e.g. customer = ' OR 1=1 --

Apply now truncates the discount (MidpointRounding.ToZero) and the result (ToZero): rounding mode silently changed from AwayFromZero and rounded twice. Example: amount 10.00 at 10.06% gives 8.99 before and 9.00 after, so the customer is charged up to a cent more.
notes: medium. Judgment call: could be argued as intentional, but it is an unannounced money behaviour change. Caught only if the review names the rounding change
high. Pure rename of _repository to _invoices, applied consistently in all 6 places

defect_description: Delete endpoint has no [RequireRole('Admin')], unlike the Update endpoint beside it: any signed-in user can delete invoices.

notes: medium-high. Adds three tests only; each asserts behaviour that matches ApprovalService (whitespace reason throws ArgumentException, unknown id throws KeyNotFoundException, approver and time recorded)

defect_description: Approve logs the whole invoice object and the whole CurrentUser session ({@Invoice}, {@Session}) at Information: customer data and user identity and role end up in application logs, which are retained and widely readable.
notes: medium. Caught if the review names sensitive data (invoice payload or session/user details) being logged. UserSession holds only username and role in this repo, so no token leak is claimed

defect_description: ConcurrentDictionary replaced by Dictionary in a repository that is registered as a singleton and shared across concurrent requests: concurrent Add/Update can corrupt the dictionary or throw. ContainsKey then set in Add is also a check-then-act race.

README says 'sign out and sign in again' resets the sample data. It does not: login and logout only create and remove sessions (AuthController.cs), invoices are untouched. README also says the demo accounts live in the in-memory store; they come from appsettings.json.
notes: low-medium. Judgment call: docs-only change, but the reset claim is checkably false. Caught only if the review names the false reset claim. The appsettings change is harmless

defect_description: New catch (Exception) returns 200 OK with { status: 'completed' } for any unexpected failure: a failed action is reported as success and the error is swallowed with no logging.

On a PayEx timeout the submitter retries the same payment submission up to three times, with no idempotency key and no status check. PayEx can time out after it has accepted the payment, so a retry can create a duplicate payment for the invoice.
notes: high. Caught if the review names a duplicate payment or a non-idempotent retry after a timeout. Retry count, backoff and cancellation handling are not the defect

high. Behaviour-preserving extract-method refactor: both paths still set status, DecidedBy and DecidedAt and call Update once; Reject sets DecisionNote beforehand. A review that asserts a behaviour change is a false alarm
